items.fact: Required property 1: non-linear, otherwise the network collapses to one linear map
items.where: Why a nonlinearity, first bullet (W2 W1 x)

items.fact: Required property 2: differentiable almost everywhere is enough, ReLU is fine
items.where: Why a nonlinearity, third bullet (autograd uses 0 at the kink)

items.fact: Sigmoid 1/(1+e^-x), output in (0,1), probability interpretation
items.where: Sigmoid and tanh table; output-layer table

items.fact: Sigmoid cons: saturates both sides, vanishing gradient; not zero-centred
items.where: Sigmoid and tanh table and 'Saturation' / 'Why zero-centred matters' paragraphs (slope at most 0.25, LeCun 1998)

items.fact: Tanh: zero-centred, gradients can be positive or negative and updates move more freely
items.where: Sigmoid and tanh table; 'Why zero-centred matters' (made precise: same-sign weight updates, zig-zag)

items.fact: Tanh cons: still saturates, vanishing gradient
items.where: Sigmoid and tanh table (slope below 0.01 beyond |x| = 3.0)

items.fact: ReLU max(0,x): trivially cheap, no saturation for x>0
items.where: The ReLU family, first paragraph

items.fact: ReLU cons: dead neurons, a unit stuck at 0 has zero gradient and never recovers
items.where: Dead units, measured: definition, animation and sweep; corrected: deeper-layer dead units can revive (measured 69 to 43)

items.fact: Leaky ReLU max(alpha x, x): ReLU benefits plus gradient on negative inputs, fixes dead neurons
items.where: The ReLU family table (Maas et al. 2013, 0.01); Dead units: leaky turns the failure into an overflow at the same rates (measured)

items.fact: Leaky ReLU cons: one more hyperparameter alpha (PReLU learns it)
items.where: The ReLU family table, Leaky and PReLU rows (He et al. 2015, init 0.25)

items.fact: Softmax e^xi / sum e^xj: sigmoid generalised to K classes, outputs a distribution
items.where: The output layer: table and 'Softmax, in four facts' (softmax([x,0]) = sigmoid(x), checked)

items.fact: Softmax cons: expensive for very large K (LM vocabularies); output-layer only
items.where: Correction box 'with a large vocabulary, the cost is the projection' (Qwen2.5-0.5B numbers); 'output-layer only' corrected in passing: softmax also normalises attention and router scores

items.fact: GELU x Phi(x), Phi Gaussian CDF; input weighted by its Gaussian probability, smooth, self-scaling; default in BERT/GPT-era transformers
items.where: Smooth rectifiers table and 'GELU's idea'; 'self-scaling' marked as unsourced in 'Why the smooth ones win'

items.fact: SiLU/Swish x sigma(x): nearly identical curve to GELU; found by architecture search, empirically beats ReLU
items.where: Correction box 'SiLU is not nearly identical to GELU, and was not found by the search' (max gap 0.193, Swish-1 = SiL of Elfwing et al.; ImageNet +0.9% / +0.6%)

items.fact: Both smooth ReLU-like curves with a small negative dip; empirically better than ReLU in transformers
items.where: Smooth rectifiers: lowest values derived; 'Why the smooth ones win' qualifies the claim with Shazeer's Table 1 (GELU/Swish alone barely beat ReLU)
